principles.text: After a really good run and in a difficult/choppy period, deliberately trade less and stay patient rather than forcing entries.
Shorting is almost always too early; wait for clear confirmation on the bearish side instead of front-running a pullback in a strong uptrend.

Prefer selling into strength on lower-cap stocks - they have weaker fundamentals, a higher chance of fading, and rarely make multi-week moves, so trailing the 9/21/50 EMA can give back ~20% before the first close below.

Decide your exit plan (trail wide for a longer move vs tighter to protect profit) before the pullback starts, by weighing potential upside against potential give-back; emotions distort the decision once profits are shrinking.
Use IWM/Russell mainly as a relative-strength/breadth tell - it tends to lag and make lower highs before a >15% correction while the QQQ is still at highs; weight QQQ more for tech focus.
Screen for liquidity: prefer >$100M (raising toward $200M) dollar volume and check the 1-/5-min chart - thin names with ~$25K-per-candle volume have wide spreads and poor fills.
